subject: general
question: A retailer allows a 22% discount on the marked price. What should be the marked price (in ₹) of an item whose cost price is ₹780, in order to make a profit of 26%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct relation between **Cost Price (CP)** and **Marked Price (MP)**: CP ÷ MP = (100 − D%) ÷ (100 + P%).

Given: **Discount (D)** = 22% and **Profit (P)** = 26%.

Ratio CP : MP = (100 − 22) : (100 + 26) = 78 : 126.

Given **CP** = ₹780, which is 78 × 10.

Multiplying the ratio by 10, **MP** = 126 × 10 = ₹1,260.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,260.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **CP** = ₹780, **Profit%** = 26%, **Discount%** = 22%.
Formulas: SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 | MP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − D%)
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7ab50568de46575b2c69aa5f55e87b78f410aa6620b0b285d9dbdfbae4b0d0e4.png] 
⇒ First, calculate **Selling Price (SP)**: SP = 780 × (126 ÷ 100) = 7.8 × 126 = ₹982.8.
⇒ Now, use the discount to find **Marked Price (MP)**: MP × (100 − 22) ÷ 100 = 982.8.
⇒ MP × 78 ÷ 100 = 982.8.
⇒ MP = (982.8 × 100) ÷ 78 = 98280 ÷ 78.
⇒ MP = ₹1,260.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,260.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

**Marked Price (MP)** is the price listed on the label. Discount is always calculated on MP: SP = MP − Discount.

Cost Price & Profit

**Cost Price (CP)** is the price at which the retailer buys. Profit is always calculated on CP: SP = CP + Profit.
